hints: Apply the binomial expansion to $(1+2x)^{-3/2}$ as far as $x^2$.
Evaluate the coefficients using $n=-3/2$, including the factor $(2x)^r$ in each term.
Multiply the resulting three-term expansion by both terms of $(2-x)$.
Discard powers above $x^2$ and simplify the remaining coefficients.
walkthrough: Apply the binomial expansion formula $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dots$ to $(1 + 2x)^{-3/2}$ with $n = -\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $u = 2x$:

Assemble the expansion of $(1 + 2x)^{-3/2}$ up to $x^2$:
$$(1 + 2x)^{-3/2} = 1 - 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2 + \dots$$

Multiply this series by $(2 - x)$:
$$(2 - x)\left(1 - 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2\right) = 2\left(1 - 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2\right) - x\left(1 - 3x + \dfrac{15}{2}x^2\right)$$

Expand and retain terms up to $x^2$:
$$= (2 - 6x + 15x^2) - (x - 3x^2) = 2 + (-6x - x) + (15x^2 + 3x^2)$$

ai_rubric.Binomial Expansion: Gives unsimplified first two terms of the expansion of $(1+2x)^{-\frac32}$, e.g. $1+(-\frac32)(2x)$. Gives unsimplified term in $x^2$, e.g. $(-\frac32)(-\frac32-1)(2x)^2/2!$. The final result is $2-7x+18x^2$.
